stream and channel lifetime (section 13.1): a Write / Listen stream classifies its opening metadata once and is decided as soon as its first request names the database, then stays admitted for its whole life; a WebChannel classifies the opening init header block the same way, binds the channel to the admitted app and the session epoch of that admission, and closes the channel when a later envelope presents a replacement token for another app or one that does not verify. Neither token expiry nor a policy change ends an admitted stream: reconnecting is a new admission

resumable upload binding (section 13.2): an enforced initiation records the admitted app and the epoch of that admission in the upload session, and every later request on that session -- continuation, status query, cancel and finalization -- must present a valid token for the same app. A refused request is refused before the command is read, so it neither advances nor deletes the upload; token expiry mid-upload therefore preserves the resumable state
off is the absence of a policy, so a service configured off structurally cannot parse a header or record an observation

the explicit bypass matrix of specification section 12.2, each surface requiring its own credential and never a path shape: the Firestore owner credential, Identity Toolkit Admin routes with the owner credential, the emulator inspection routes with the control token, the Storage JSON API dialect with the owner credential, and a Storage download URL whose token binds in constant time to the resolved bucket, object name and generation

denial before Security Rules and before every side effect: no user, no issued or rotated credential, no consumed OOB or phone code, no MFA change, no object generation, no upload session, no Firestore mutation and no rules document-access budget consumption

the error contract of section 17: PERMISSION_DENIED with the public code in fireemu-code metadata on gRPC, HTTP 403 Google JSON on Firestore REST and on Auth, and the Firebase Storage JSON error envelope with 403 on Storage; the public code is APP_CHECK_REQUIRED or APP_CHECK_INVALID and never the detailed reason

a project without a static appCheck.apps registration cannot use App Check at all, so an enforced service denies every request that targets it; this is the fail-closed reading of specification section 14

absence of a ruleset is not a bypass: the owner credential is verified by the App Check path itself, because with Security Rules disabled every Firestore caller is otherwise treated as the owner without presenting anything

the Storage JSON API dialect and the emulator inspection routes bypass Security Rules and their own guard more loosely than they bypass App Check (unauthenticated JSON API traffic, and an emulator route without an Origin); the App Check bypass requires the credential in both cases, so an enforced service cannot be defeated by rewriting a path
